subject: Cholesky model runs in 'usermodel' but not 'enrich'

messages.author: 424edea90949f8a3
messages.subject: Cholesky model runs in 'usermodel' but not 'enrich'
parts:
I am running stratified Genomic SEM on two contrasting models, one common factor (F_common) model and one Cholesky model for a unique factor (F_unique). The following code for F_common gives expected results:

model <- ("F_common =~ 1 * trait1 + NA * trait2
          F_common ~~ NA * F_common

          trait1 ~~ 0*trait1
          trait2 ~~ 0*trait2")

penrich <- enrich(s_covstruc= gen_cov,
                  model=model,
                  params="F_common ~~ F_common")

However, the following model does not run, throwing 'Results_List not found': 

model <- ("F_common =~ 1 * trait1 + NA * trait2
            F_unique =~ 1 * trait1

            F_common ~~ 0 * F_unique
            F_common ~~ NA * F_common
            F_unique ~~ NA * F_unique

            trait1 ~~ 0 * trait2
            trait1 ~~ 0 * trait1
            trait2 ~~ 0 * trait2")

penrich <- enrich(s_covstruc= gen_cov,
                  model=model,
                  params="F_unique ~~ F_unique")

I've tried a bunch of different variations but haven't been able to figure out what's the problem. Also, running it in usermodel (using the 'ldscoutput' genetic covariance matrix in the complete genome) this model runs without issues. Hoping that someone can enlighten me!

messages.author: d6d83e22ef3ba9f1
messages.subject: Re: Cholesky model runs in 'usermodel' but not 'enrich'
parts:
Hi Joelle, 

Thanks for raising this issue. The problem is that the default behavior for the enrich function is to freely estimate the parameters that are not the factor loadings (e.g., the residual variances of trait 1 and 2) within each annotation, which causes the model not to be identified when you are running a Cholesky model like you have here. I added an update to the enrich function a few months ago when I noticed the same issue that allows you to override this behavior using an argument called fixparam. To get your model to run you would want to write the following code where you fix the parameters that you want set to 0. I have also found that using unit variance identification works a bit better as far as getting these stratified models to converge, so have also added std.lv=TRUE as an argument and removed the code in the model syntax that you had that used the unit loading identification: 

model <- ("F_common =~ trait1 + trait2
            F_unique =~ trait1

trait1 ~~ 0 * trait1
            trait2 ~~ 0 * trait2")

params="F_unique ~~ F_unique",fixparam=fixparam,std.lv=TRUE)

Best, 
  Andrew
